subject: Token envelope & demo scope — next steps and sizing clarifications
messages:
From: James Park <james.park@shopline.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — Shopline recommendation assistant (post-call)

Hi Irene / Marissa / Markus,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team found the latency/streaming examples helpful. Quick recap from our side to make sure we're aligned on the pilot workload and SLO targets: 

- Traffic shape: bursty shopping hours 11:00-18:00 PT, steady lower traffic overnight.
- Peak windows: ~120 QPS sustained for 10-15 minute windows during promos; baseline steady-state ~8–12 QPS.
- Request mix: 70% single-turn prompts (avg ~450 tokens processed), 30% multi-turn chat sessions where KV cache is relevant (avg 1.6 turns/session).
- Streaming: we need partial token streaming to the browser for chat sessions; soft target latency for first token ~120ms, tail latency 95th < 600ms.
- Cost sensitivity: we'd prefer a quantized/efficient model variant if quality holds; goal is to keep hosted cost within the attached estimate.

Next steps from Shopline: please confirm the pilot envelope you recommend (tokens/sec, QPS headroom, concurrency assumptions) and any altered SLOs we should expect in a hosted vs dedicated environment. We also included a small sample payload (attached) showing typical session lengths.

Thanks — happy to schedule a short replay if that helps.

—James
James Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Shopline
james.park@shopline.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — Shopline recommendation assistant (post-call)

Hi James — great notes, thank you. Short post-call recap + clarifying questions and proposed pilot envelope below.

Recap (from our side):
- We saw the same burst pattern in the call (promo windows driving 10–15 minute peaks).
- Streaming + KV cache for multi-turn flows will be important for latency and token savings.
- You flagged cost sensitivity — we can propose an efficient model variant for the pilot and compare quality on your eval set.

Clarifying questions (quick):
1) When you say 120 QPS peak, is that concurrent socket connections or completed request QPS? (affects connection concurrency vs infer concurrency).
2) For multi-turn sessions, what's the average context length you want preserved in cache (in tokens)?
3) Are partial-token streaming (first-token flush) requirements mandatory for the pilot or preferred?

Proposed pilot envelope (hosted):
- Baseline: 12 QPS steady-state, average 450 tokens/request => ~5.4k tokens/sec steady-state.
- Peak headroom: plan for a 12x peak factor => 65k tokens/sec for the 10–15 minute windows (this includes a safety margin and burst buffering).
- Concurrency assumptions: average outstanding requests 1.6 per connection during promo windows -> plan for ~2000 concurrent streams for socket-level capacity planning.
- Streaming: enable partial-token flush on first 50–150ms for chat flows (first-token latency target 120–150ms in hosted tier; 95th token latency we expect ~400–700ms depending on model variant).

Attachments I'm sending: demo-workload-spec.csv (CSV with QPS/token distribution) — see attached. We'll also run a short synthetic to validate the envelope prior to the pilot.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to run a quick capacity sketch (synthetic) using the sample traffic (Marissa, can you run this and put the results in the Drive link?).
- Shopline to confirm answers to the clarifying questions above.
- We'll share a targeted pilot SLO doc and hosted vs dedicated cost delta by EOD tomorrow.

Open to a 20-min sync later today if you'd like — I have 3:30–4:00 PT free.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Attachment: demo-workload-spec.csv (text/csv, 3 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, James Park <james.park@shopline.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — Shopline recommendation assistant (post-call)

Thanks — quick note on the capacity sketch I ran locally against James' sample. Summary below; I will upload the full csv to the Drive link.

- Synthetic assumptions: 450 avg tokens/request, Pareto burst shape, 12 QPS baseline, 120 QPS peak windows.
- Token/sec sizing: baseline ~5.4k tokens/sec; 12x peak => 65k tokens/sec.
- Model choice: Recommend starting with an 8-bit quantized medium-size model variant for the pilot to balance cost and tail latency; we can A/B with the full-precision model on a small subset of traffic.
- Observed latency (local sketch, simulated network): first-token median ~110ms, 95th ~520ms at the target envelope using a 3x accelerator pool with prefix caching enabled.
- Concurrency: during peaks we measured ~1.8 outstanding requests/connection; planning for 2200 concurrent streams is reasonable.

Action items from me:
- I'll upload the synthetic run CSV and the rough cost delta sheet to the Drive link by 12:30 PT.
- Recommend we schedule the pilot kickoff once Shopline confirms the clarifying answers Irene asked about (especially whether 120 QPS is socket-level).

Marissa
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: James Park <james.park@shopline.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 13:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — Shopline recommendation assistant (post-call)

Thanks Irene / Marissa — this is great and aligns with our expectations. Short answers: 

- 120 QPS is completed requests QPS (not socket concurrency). During promos we see many quick-fire requests from clients so concurrency spikes too; we'll confirm exact socket counts in the follow-up.
- For multi-turn sessions keep a conservative 1024 token cache per user session for the pilot.
- Partial-token streaming preferred but not mandatory for the first two weeks; we can enable it for the critical promo windows and iterate.

Let's lock the pilot envelope you proposed (baseline 12 QPS / ~5.4k tokens/sec, peak headroom targeting 65k tokens/sec, plan for ~2.2k concurrent streams). We'll aim to stand up the synthetic test tomorrow morning and hand off logs for a quick validation run.

I'll accept the 3:30 PT slot for a short pilot kickoff — see you then.

—James
